styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ruined timber-framed house, the same kind as the references. Its tile roof has several lightness steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) with scalloped per-tile texture. The collapsed hole shows exposed rafters, and creeping vines and grass add variation. Walls have plaster speckle and timber frames, and the windows are broken. Measured: 23 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 2% near-flat coverage against 0%, and only 4% of dark edge pixels near-neutral. That means the outlines are tinted dark brown and red-brown rather than a black sticker line. It is slightly less crisp than the references in the wall shading, but not shallower, and density is at or above the references.
